FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
A Vermont resident must register any vehicle driven on the roads, and a person moving in from another state must register the vehicle within sixty days of moving into Vermont [A01].
Why it matters: Sixty days, the same clock as the license.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Proof of valid registration must always be in the vehicle while it is in use and a police officer has the right to see it [A01].
Why it matters: Registration rides in the car.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Registration plates must be firmly attached so they cannot loosen, no part may be covered or hidden, they must be kept clean, and the rear plate must be lit so it can be read from at least fifty feet away [A01].
Why it matters: Fifty feet of rear plate legibility.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
The number plates issued for a vehicle may be used only on that vehicle, but you may transfer them to a new vehicle you buy when you trade in or sell the old one [A01].
Why it matters: Plates belong to the vehicle but can follow a trade.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
When selling a vehicle give the buyer a bill of sale with the buyer's name, the seller's signature, the date, and the vehicle's year, make, serial number and sale price, sign the back of the title with the new owner's name and address, the mileage and the date, and remove your plates [A01].
Why it matters: Bill of sale contents and the title step.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
An odometer statement signed by both seller and buyer is required on every sale of a vehicle of model year twenty eleven or newer, and the statement is part of the title or the Vermont bill of sale [A01].
Why it matters: Twenty eleven is the odometer statement cutoff.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
When trading vehicles exchange bills of sale, have the title to the vehicle you receive signed over to you, remove your plates from the old vehicle and put them on the new one if you transfer the registration, and mail the registration, tax and title application with the title and fees to the DMV in Montpelier within twenty-four hours [A01].
Why it matters: Twenty-four hours to mail the trade paperwork.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
A lost registration certificate can be replaced at any DMV office, by mail or online [A01].
Why it matters: Three replacement channels.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A02
If one or both registration plates are lost, a Replacement Plate Application is available at any DMV office, at a police station or online [A02].
Why it matters: Police stations stock the plate form.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A02
A change of your name, your address or the color of your vehicle must be reported to the DMV within thirty days [A02].
Why it matters: Even a repaint must be reported within thirty days.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A02
Buying a new or used non leased vehicle triggers the purchase and use tax of six percent of the price paid or the current fair market value, whichever is greater [A02].
Why it matters: Six percent of the higher figure.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A02
A new resident registering a vehicle acquired outside Vermont on which they or their spouse already paid a sales or use tax is exempt from the Vermont tax when the tax paid elsewhere equals or exceeds Vermont's, or when the vehicle was registered for at least three years in a jurisdiction that collects such a tax, and otherwise owes the difference [A02].
Why it matters: Credit for tax paid elsewhere, three year rule.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A02
A leased vehicle from a Vermont dealer must be registered with a purchase and use tax computation form or the lease agreement or dealer worksheet, and without them the vehicle is taxed at six percent of the acquisition cost [A02].
Why it matters: Missing lease paperwork means tax on full cost.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A02
The taxable cost of a leased vehicle is six percent of the acquisition cost minus the lease end value as stated in the computation form, lease agreement or dealer worksheet, regardless of whether there is an option to buy at lease end [A02].
Why it matters: Lease tax subtracts the residual value.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A02
Every vehicle must have a Vermont motor vehicle title, with exceptions such as a motorcycle under three hundred cubic centimeters of engine displacement and a trailer with an empty weight of fifteen hundred pounds or less [A02].
Why it matters: Two title exemptions with numbers.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
A Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin is required for every new vehicle and no new vehicle can be registered without it, and any vehicle registered in Vermont needs a registration application, the bill of sale and the former owner's title signed over [A02].
Why it matters: Three documents for registration.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A03
A vehicle identification number is a unique seventeen character code of digits and capital letters that identifies a specific vehicle and its features, specifications and manufacturer, and before nineteen eighty-one such numbers varied from eleven to seventeen characters [A03].
Why it matters: Seventeen characters since nineteen eighty-one.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A03
Vehicle identification number verification is required for vehicles with salvage documentation, vehicles being titled under bond and vehicles registered in any foreign country including Canada, and it must be done in Vermont by a law enforcement officer, supervised law enforcement personnel or a designated DMV employee [A03].
Why it matters: Three triggers and who may verify.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A03
A vehicle registered in Vermont with a salvage title receives a title marked rebuilt vehicle, and registering it requires having the identification number checked by a DMV employee or Vermont law enforcement with the verification section of the application completed [A03].
Why it matters: Salvage becomes rebuilt after verification.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A03
Borrowing money from a bank, credit union or another person to buy a vehicle puts a lien on it, the lender is the lien holder whose name must be on the registration application, and the title is sent to the lien holder and withheld from you until the loan is repaid [A03].
Why it matters: The lender holds the title.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A03
Vermont's maintenance of financial responsibility law requires the vehicle you drive to be covered by liability insurance, and liability and property damage coverage protect you from financial loss when bodily injury or property damage occurs [A03].
Why it matters: Liability insurance is mandatory.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A03
Coverage must be at least twenty-five thousand dollars for death or injury of one person, fifty thousand dollars for death or injury of two or more persons and ten thousand dollars for property damage [A03].
Why it matters: The three minimum amounts.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A03
You must carry an insurance card from your insurer in the vehicle showing the vehicle is covered, and must show it when stopped by a police officer and when taking a driving test [A03].
Why it matters: Two occasions that require the card.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A03
A driver stopped without insurance receives a ticket, a fine and two points on the driving record, while an insured driver who cannot show the card at the stop has fifteen days to produce a card proving coverage at the time of the stop [A03].
Why it matters: Two points uninsured, fifteen days to show a card.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A04
Driving without insurance and then having a crash even if not at fault, driving under the influence, taking a vehicle without consent, driving while suspended, revoked or refused, causing a death or leaving a crash scene costs you the license until you get insurance, with proof required for a full three years [A04].
Why it matters: Three years of proof after any listed event.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A04
A vehicle must be inspected once a year and kept running properly at all times, a badly running vehicle can put you at fault in a crash, the sticker shows when the next inspection is due, and a newly registered vehicle must be inspected within fifteen days unless it already bears a valid Vermont sticker [A04].
Why it matters: Yearly inspection, fifteen days after registration.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A04
Driving fifty-five or sixty miles per hour on the interstate instead of sixty-five saves fuel, and the Environmental Protection Agency estimates up to a fifteen percent improvement in fuel economy from that tip alone [A04].
Why it matters: Handbook fuel statistic, stated as the handbook states it.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A04
Accelerating smoothly from a stop and braking softly saves fuel, while fast starts, weaving and hard braking waste fuel and wear brakes and tires faster, so keep a safe distance and anticipate traffic to brake and accelerate gradually [A04].
Why it matters: Smoothness saves fuel and parts.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A04
Idling wastes fuel, wears the engine and can cause respiratory illness, so clear snow and ice before starting, limit stationary warm ups to about thirty seconds when possible, and in town idling more than ten seconds uses more fuel than shutting off and restarting [A04].
Why it matters: Thirty seconds warm up, ten seconds idle threshold.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A04
Leaving a vehicle idling unattended in public violates Vermont's unattended motor vehicle law, so if you leave the vehicle you must shut it off [A04].
Why it matters: Unattended idling is illegal.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A04
Keeping tires at the recommended pressure shown on the driver's door jamb placard and in the owner's manual can cut average fuel use by three to four percent, while under inflated tires raise rolling resistance, lower fuel economy and wear faster [A04].
Why it matters: Three to four percent from tire pressure.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A05
Keep the engine tuned, the wheels aligned and the air filters replaced as recommended, and carry no unnecessary weight such as trunk clutter or heavy roof luggage, because misaligned wheels and extra weight make the engine work harder and burn more fuel [A05].
Why it matters: Maintenance and weight tips.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A05
Use heating and air conditioning selectively, since cutting air conditioner use when temperatures exceed eighty degrees can save ten to fifteen percent of fuel, prefer the vent setting and park in the shade [A05].
Why it matters: Ten to fifteen percent from the air conditioner.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A05
Drive with the windows closed unless your speed stays under fifty miles per hour, because open windows at highway speed add aerodynamic drag and lower fuel economy, and consolidate trips and car pool to save miles and fuel [A05].
Why it matters: Fifty is the open window threshold.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0070]

Misconceptions:
- Plates belong to the owner and can go on any car: false, plates are for one vehicle, though they may transfer to a replacement vehicle when the old one is sold or traded.
- Having insurance is enough even without the card: false, the card must be in the vehicle, shown at stops and tests, and a missing card must be produced within fifteen days.
- A repainted car needs no DMV notice: false, a color change, like a name or address change, must be reported within thirty days.
- Idling in the driveway to warm up is efficient: false, warm ups should be about thirty seconds, driving gently warms the engine best, and unattended idling in public is illegal.
- The purchase tax is always on the price paid: false, it is six percent of the price or fair market value, whichever is greater.

Mnemonics:
- Twenty-five, fifty, ten: one person, two or more, property.
- Sixty to register, thirty to update, fifteen to inspect: the three ownership deadlines in days.
- Six percent of the bigger number: the purchase and use tax.

Glossary:
- Purchase and use tax: the six percent tax paid when a vehicle is bought, based on price or fair market value, whichever is greater
- Lien holder: the lender whose name goes on the registration and who holds the title until the vehicle loan is repaid
- Maintenance of financial responsibility: the Vermont law requiring liability insurance on any vehicle driven
- Rebuilt vehicle title: the title issued in Vermont to a vehicle that previously carried a salvage title
- Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin: the document required to register any new vehicle

Dynamic facts isolated:
- The DMV phone number, web address and office locations named on these pages are contact details that can change and are not carried as knowledge facts.
